text:
The Economic Crime Levy applies to businesses that are supervised under the Money Laundering Regulations.

Who does not need to register with HMRC

You do not need to register with HMRC for the Economic Crime Levy if you are supervised under the Money Laundering Regulations by any of the following collection authorities:

the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA)

the Gambling Commission

both HMRC and the FCA

both HMRC and the Gambling Commission

You will need to follow the FCA or Gambling Commission guidance and pay the levy to one of these collection authorities.

Do not register for the Economic Crime Levy, submit yearly Economic Crime Levy returns, or pay the Economic Crime Levy to HMRC.

Who needs to register with HMRC

You must register with HMRC if the sum of your UK revenue is more than £10.2 million for all accounting periods ending within a financial year, and your business is regulated either by:

HMRC for anti-money laundering purposes

a professional body for anti-money laundering purposes

The financial year runs from 1 April to 31 March of the following year.

If your accounting period is not 12 months, the £10.2 million threshold is amended pro rata using the number of days in the relevant accounting periods.

You only need to register for the Economic Crime Levy once, but you will need to submit a return and pay the levy each year.

If you are part of a business group

The levy will only apply to members in the group who meet the requirements for registering.

Each eligible member of the business group must register, submit yearly returns, and pay for the Economic Crime Levy separately.

If you are part of a partnership

The nominated partner must register, submit yearly returns, and pay for the Economic Crime Levy on behalf of the partnership.
